rhythm.value: 46.17 s at 30 fps. Detector: 41 shots, 40 cuts, median 0.93 s, 52 cuts a minute. Corrected (5 splits, 7 rejected boundaries): 39 shots, 38 cuts, median hold 0.97 s, mean 1.18 s, p10 0.40 s, p90 2.03 s, range 0.23-3.07 s, 49.4 cuts a minute. Three tempos inside one film: (1) 0-2.43 s hook, five changes in 1.27 s (holds 0.40, 0.30, 0.33, 0.23 s); (2) type and kinetic shots at 0.7-1.3 s each, one line or one idea per hold; (3) interface walkthroughs held longer (1.6-3.1 s) with their own internal motion (scrolls, cursor, push-ins), so the eye reads the product while the edit rests. The ground alternates on hard cuts between cream #F2F4E9 (or interface white #F6F6F6) and near-black brown #201A16: of 39 corrected shots 23 sit on a light ground, 11 on the dark one and 5 on a photograph or a window framed on dark; 18 of 38 cuts change that ground class (frame borders sampled at each shot's middle), which does the work a transition effect would otherwise do. Four cuts land on one frame of bare ground before the next element (F132, F959, F1010, F1298), a one-frame breath. No dissolves, no whips: every picture change is a hard cut; all motion is inside shots. Words inside a line arrive every 2 frames (0.067 s) with a 3-4 frame rise. Sound: I cannot hear it. audio.json has no tempo (librosa unavailable, RMS fallback), so no beat grid is built. Detector cuts on onsets 27.5% vs 21.2% chance (lift 1.3). Corrected cuts on onsets (±0.08 s): 12 of 38 = 31.6% vs 21.2% chance (lift 1.49). Per section: hook and opening 0-8.1 s 4 of 8 (50%) vs 40% chance; interface middle 8.1-27.2 s 2 of 14 (14%) vs 18% chance; closing 27.2-44.5 s 6 of 16 (38%) vs 18% chance (lift 2.1). Onset density 1.39 per second, so the ratios are readable. Loudness swells (50 ms RMS, local maximum over ±0.3 s, above 1.35x median): 54, median spacing 0.45 s, many exactly 0.40 s apart (a pulse near 150 BPM is possible but bounded below by the 0.3 s window, so not established); 11 of 38 cuts within 0.1 s of a swell vs 23% chance: no evidence. Loudness per second is 0.4-0.8x the median until 9 s, then 1.1-1.4x from the first interface shot onwards, dipping at 16 s and 27 s, and falling to 0.27x by 45 s: the track's lift coincides with the product's first appearance (inferred: the drop was placed under the dashboard). Transferable rule: the late section cuts on transients more often than chance; the interface section does not follow the sound at all.

value.name: type-on-photo-flash
value.description: The key word of the opening sentence is typed letter by letter in yellow #F6E977 on #201A16 from F35, one letter every 2 frames (g F35, gl F37, glo F39, glob F41, globa F43), the glyphs growing about 15% as they type. On the frame the word completes (F45) the ground cuts to a crowd photograph and the word turns white at the same place and size (about 0.58 frame width); a second crowd photograph replaces it at F56; at F66 the yellow word on dark returns for 7 frames, and F73 cuts to cream for the next clause. Holds: 10, 10, 11, 7 frames.
value.why: The eye never moves: the word stays in one place and size while four grounds change under it, so the viewer reads one idea while being shown its scale (many people). Typing at 2 frames a letter makes the first second about anticipation of the word; the photo flash pays it off in 0.7 s, too fast to read as stock footage.

value.name: dot-to-wordmark
value.description: F132 is an empty dark frame. F133-F138: a dot at frame centre grows to a pale-blue #DBECFD disc about 13% of frame width (6 frames, decelerating). F140-F152: the mark is wiped in inside the disc in stepped slices (12 frames), held to F158. F159: the mark vanishes; F160-F166 the disc travels right about 0.2 frame width while the first letters of the wordmark wipe in from the left behind it; F167-F176 the disc shrinks and breaks into the remaining letters, ending as the full stop; a small sub-line fades in under it F174-F176. The wordmark sits yellow until F192, flips to white at F193, and holds to the cut at F203.
value.why: One shape carries the attention from a point to the full name: the viewer watches the disc, and the disc becomes the punctuation, so the eye ends where the name ends. The late yellow-to-white flip says 'settled' without another move.

value.name: mirrored-object-layout-cut
value.description: Shot A (F373-F407): a disc carrying a currency symbol (about 0.18 frame height) rises from lower right on a thick yellow trail of the same width, settling in 5 frames (F373-F378) then drifting up slowly; text left-aligned at x 0.06 builds word by word; the symbol swaps once after 17 frames (F390). Cut at F408: the layout is mirrored, the disc descending from top left on its trail, the text right of centre; its symbol swaps after 16 frames (F424). Then F441 cuts to a single centred line.
value.why: Mirroring keeps the layout familiar while reversing direction, so the second clause reads as a continuation, not a new scene. The symbol swap inside each hold says 'any' without listing anything; the trail gives the object a path, so the eye follows motion rather than searching the frame.

value.name: word-split-insert
value.description: F930 cuts to dark with a yellow verb split in two staggered halves (left half low, right half high, about 0.2 frame height). F931-F936: a tilted interface card (about 0.3 frame width, rotated in depth about 8-10 degrees) flies up from the bottom between the halves and settles flat; the halves level onto one baseline and part to frame it. F959: one empty cream frame. F960: the same verb whole in dark ink, about 0.12 frame height. F976-F980: its halves part to open a gap about 0.08 frame width (5 frames, accelerating). F981 cuts on the open gap to dark: an outlined pill with an arrow sits where the gap was, a small word above it; F982-F983 the pill widens and fills with two flag chips; the right chip swaps at F993 and again by F1009.
value.why: The verb is literally opened to show what it does: the product sits inside the word, then the gap becomes the connector (the arrow pill). The viewer's eye is parked in the gap before the cut, so the new element appears exactly where they are looking.

value.name: countdown-behind-word
value.description: F1010 is an empty dark frame. F1011: a white word centred (about 0.1 frame height) with, behind it, a giant counter (number plus unit, about 0.6 frame height) in dim olive-yellow at roughly 35% strength and heavily blurred. The counter ticks down on F1011, F1013, F1015, F1018, F1022 (steps of 2, 2, 3, 4 frames: decelerating), lands on zero and holds 13 frames with a soft glow, then F1036 hard-cuts to a white interface.
value.why: The claim is proved by time itself: the count runs in under half a second under a word that never moves. Decelerating steps make zero land like a stop, which is the whole message.
